findings.title: Sender check crashes for integrations without sender metadata
findings.body: The check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. Integrations created before this metadata was recorded, or created through build_integration when state did not contain a sender, do not have that key. Linking such an existing-but-unattached GitHub integration to an organization therefore raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of completing the installation or showing the intended installation-failed page.

findings.title: Authenticated-user validation is bypassed when the Integration row does not yet exist
findings.body: When Integration.objects.get() raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation immediately advances the pipeline without comparing pipeline state github_authenticated_user to the GitHub app installer. Because the Integration row is normally created by an asynchronous GitHub installation webhook, a user who completes the Sentry pipeline before that webhook is processed (or when the webhook is missed/delayed) bypasses the new validation entirely, and build_integration does not fetch the installer identity from GitHub to perform the check later. This leaves a race-dependent hole in the security control added by this PR.

findings.title: GitHub token exchange and user lookup failures are not converted to the installation error page
findings.body: safe_urlopen is called outside the try/except, which only covers safe_urlread, and get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) at line 434 is also unguarded. Network errors, GitHub 5xx responses, or failures from the /user lookup can therefore propagate as unhandled exceptions and produce a 500 during installation instead of the PR's intended generic 'Invalid installation request' failure page.
